{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. Of the 19 findings, 12 are compliant, 7 require attention (6 deviations and 1 needing internal review only), and several of the deviations sit squarely in walk-away territory.

The agreement contains a strong Customer-favourable core: ownership of Customer Data and Deliverables (§ 14), assignment and change-of-control freedom (§ 24), termination for convenience with pro-rata refund (§ 9.4), audit limits (§ 22), New York law and venue (§ 28), the renewal mechanic and uplift cap (§ 8.2–8.3), and Vendor insurance (§ 18). No liquidated damages, MFN or non-solicit obligations bind us.

However, six provisions fail their fallback positions on material terms, and five of those are walk-away items:

1. **No Vendor indemnity at all** — § 20 contains only a broad one-way Customer indemnity, and § 9.3 cross-references infringement remedies in a "§ 20.5" that does not exist.
2. **One-month liability cap "without exception"** — § 21.1 sets the mutual cap at a single month's Fees and overrides the Excluded Claims in § 21.3.
3. **Full-term exclusivity on us** — § 2.2 makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider with no cap or performance exit, contradicting § 12.3.
4. **24-month post-term non-compete on us** — § 12.4, unlimited in scope and territory, again contradicting § 12.3.
5. **Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay** — § 2.1, expressly "without reduction or termination rights," conflicting with § 9.4, § 12.3 and § 7.1 with no precedence clause to resolve it.
6. **Immediate deletion, no transition assistance** — § 11.1 contradicts the otherwise compliant § 11.2/11.3 mechanics.

A further deviation on the Services licence grant (§ 13.1, excluding Affiliates and contractors and revocable at Vendor's discretion) and the 15-day Deliverable warranty (§ 19.2) round out the redlines.

We also note a recurring drafting problem: the agreement has two provisions numbered 2.2, no order-of-precedence clause, and multiple internal contradictions (§ 2.1 vs. § 9.4; § 2.2 and § 12.4 vs. § 12.3; § 11.1 vs. § 11.2–11.3; § 9.3 vs. the absent § 20.5). These conflicts should be resolved on their face rather than left to interpretation.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 20.1 (and absent § 20.5) |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 21.1 |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1–14.4 (with § 13.2, § 15.1) |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 (first of two so numbered) |
| 5 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 |
| 7 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1–24.4 (with § 13.3, § 9.2) |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 9.4 (with § 27.3, § 24.4) |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (vs. § 11.2–11.3) |
| 12 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1–22.3 |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1–28.3 |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3 (with § 7.1, § 8.3) |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2–8.3 |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 12.3 |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1–18.2 |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following provisions fall within walk-away territory under the playbook. Each must be resolved before signature.

1. **§ 20 — No Vendor indemnity, one-way Customer indemnity.** There is no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the agreement for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, while § 20.1 requires us to indemnify Vendor for "every claim relating in any way" to our use of the Services. The fallback is unmet. § 9.3 already assumes infringement remedies "required by Section 20.5" that do not exist, confirming the gap. **Position:** add the preferred Vendor indemnity with usual exclusions, standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies as a new § 20.5; narrow our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of law.

2. **§ 21.1 — One-month liability cap "without exception."** The cap is mutual but set at Fees actually paid in a single month, below the six-month walk-away floor and well below the 12-month fallback; "Fees" also excludes one-time implementation charges. "Without exception" overrides § 21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap with no super-cap, and § 21.4's savings language does not cure the quantum. **Position:** mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with Excluded Claims expressly outside the cap. § 21.2 and § 21.3 are otherwise acceptable and left intact.

3. **§ 2.2 — Full-term exclusivity.** Vendor is our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category limitation, no 12-month cap and no performance-based exit. This also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity commitment. **Position:** non-exclusive supply, confirming our freedom to source from third parties. **Fallback:** narrowed 12-month category exclusivity terminating automatically on missed service levels.

4. **§ 12.4 — 24-month post-term non-compete on Customer.** Covers "any product or service that competes with Vendor" in "any territory," with no carve-out for internal development and an express bar on acquisitions. Walk-away on both duration (exceeding 12 months post-term) and scope. It contradicts § 12.3 directly. **Position:** delete § 12.4 and let § 12.3 govern. **Fallback:** single named product, term only, with carve-outs.

5. **§ 2.1 — Three-year take-or-pay, USD 2,000,000 per year, "without reduction or termination rights."** This is the playbook's walk-away position and falls well short of the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty). It contradicts § 9.4, § 12.3 and § 7.1, and with no order-of-precedence clause it could be read to override them. **Position:** replace with pay-for-use language. **Fallback:** 12-month commitment, reducible, with true-up.

6. **§ 11.1 — Immediate deletion with no export or migration support.** As the first-listed provision it contradicts and could be read to override the otherwise compliant § 11.2/11.3 mechanics, and provides no transition-assistance period at all, failing even the 90-day fallback. **Position:** up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, with deletion subject to the § 11.2/11.3 return and certification mechanics. **Fallback:** 90 days.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline covering the six deviations.** Priority order: § 20 (Vendor indemnity plus new § 20.5), § 21.1 (cap and Excluded Claims), § 2.1 (take-or-pay), § 2.2 (exclusivity), § 12.4 (non-compete deletion), § 11.1 (transition), together with § 13.1 (extend the Services licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove revocation at Vendor's discretion) and § 19.2 (extend the Deliverable conformity warranty from 15 to 90 days, preserving the § 19.4 remedy).

2. **Treat the five walk-away items as gating.** We should not recommend signature while § 20, § 21.1, § 2.1, § 2.2, § 12.4 and § 11.1 stand as drafted. Fallbacks are available on exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitment and transition where commercially required; the indemnity and cap positions have no acceptable fallback at the current drafting.

3. **Fix the numbering and add an order-of-precedence clause.** There are two provisions numbered 2.2 and no precedence clause. We should renumber and add precedence language so the Customer-favourable provisions (§ 9.4, § 12.3, § 7.1, § 11.2–11.3) cannot be overridden by the conflicting terms.

4. **Repair the broken cross-reference in § 9.3.** It relies on infringement remedies "required by Section 20.5," which do not exist; our proposed new § 20.5 resolves this.

5. **Close out the NOSOLICIT finding internally.** The finding records that no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant binds us anywhere in the agreement, and that § 12.3 runs in our favour by preserving our right to hire anyone responding to general recruitment. The deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) failed only because they look for terms inside a restrictive covenant that does not exist. No redline or counterparty comment is proposed; we should record the verification override in the file.

6. **Confirm the § 19.2 / § 6.1 interaction on the extended warranty.** The 15-day warranty currently expires at essentially the same time as the 15-business-day acceptance window in § 6.1, leaving no post-acceptance protection; the 90-day proposal should be checked against the acceptance mechanic as drafted.

7. **Preserve the compliant provisions unchanged.** We should not reopen § 14 (IP), § 24 (assignment), § 9.4 (convenience termination), § 22 (audit), § 28 (governing law and venue), § 8.2–8.3 (renewal) or § 18 (insurance), each of which meets or exceeds our preferred position."}
